answer: One defense is vouching with liability: a new agent can only enter through an established sponsor, and the sponsor posts a bond that is slashed if the newcomer is later caught colluding. Picture a wharf where every arrival must be signed in by someone already on the ridge of good standing. An attacker spawning a thousand puppets needs a thousand sponsorships, each exposing real stake, so the cost delta between one honest identity and a fake army grows with every puppet instead of staying near zero.
